Blood oxygen levels measure how much oxygen your red blood cells are carrying. This metric indicates how well your lungs, heart, and circulatory system are working.
Heart rate variability (HRV), the variance in time between heartbeats, is an indicator of how well your body can perform and adapt to its environment.
Respiratory rate (RR), the amount of breaths you take per minute while at rest, is a general indicator of cardiovascular fitness.
Resting heart rate (RHR), the number of times your heart beats per minute when at rest, is an indicator of cardiovascular health.
Skin temperature, the temperature of the surface of your body, indicates how your body is regulating heat and varies day-to-day, unlike your core body temperature.

"A high heart rate, or tachycardia, means your heart is beating too fast to get an accurate ECG reading. WHOOP can only check for AFib with heart rates between 50 - 150 beats per minute.
A high heart rate could be due to exercise, stress, nervousness, fever, effects of alcohol, caffeine, dehydration, infection, AFib, or another type of arrhythmia.
Make sure you are in a state of rest/calm before taking an ECG reading. If this result does not feel normal for you, or if you are experiencing heart palpitations, lightheadedness or other symptoms please seek medical advice."

"An inconclusive result means the recording could not be classified. This is typically due to insufficient signal quality which could be due to the band being too loose or you may have been moving too much. This could also be due to irregularity in the signal that does not meet the classification for AFib or High and Low HR.
Try taking the ECG reading again ensuring you are following the instructions carefully for best results. If you get inconclusive recordings repeatedly please seek medical advice.
Based on this reading it’s not possible to determine whether AFib is detected or not, so if you are experiencing symptoms or repeatedly get an inconclusive result please seek medical advice."

"A low heart rate, or bradycardia, means your heart is beating too slowly to get an accurate ECG reading. WHOOP can only check for AFib with heart rates between 50 - 150 beats per minute.
A heart rate can be low because of certain medications, training to be an elite athlete, or due to an irregular heart rhythm.
If this result does not feel normal for you, or if you are experiencing lightheadedness, shortness of breath, or other symptoms please seek medical advice."

A No AFib - High Heart Rate result means no signs of atrial fibrillation were detected but your heart rate is higher than normal (more than 100 BPM). A high heart rate could be due to exercise, stress, nervousness, fever, alcohol, caffeine, dehydration, infection, or other arrhythmia.

A normal sinus rhythm result means your heart is beating in a uniform pattern. This happens when the upper and lower chambers of the heart are beating in sync. It does not guarantee that you’re healthy or don’t have a heart condition. If you’re not feeling well or are experiencing any symptoms, you should talk to your doctor.

"Atrial Fibrillation - High Heart Rate result means there were signs of atrial fibrillation and high heart rate detected.
Atrial fibrillation means your heart is beating in an irregular pattern with the upper and lower chambers of the heart out of sync. AFib is the most common form of arrhythmia, or irregular heart rhythm. If you receive an AFib classification and you have not been diagnosed with AFib, you should talk to your doctor.
With this result, high heart rate means your heart is beating between 100-150 bpm, which is higher than is considered normal while at rest. WHOOP cannot detect AFib in heart rates that are over 150 bmp.
With both AFib detected and a high heart rate, it’s best to consult your doctor to get further advice."

"An Atrial Fibrillation (AFib) result means your heart is beating in an irregular pattern with the upper and lower chambers of the heart out of sync.
AFib is the most common form of arrhythmia, or irregular heart rhythm. If you receive an AFib classification and you have not been diagnosed with AFib, you should talk to your doctor. The WHOOP ECG app can check for AFib between 51 and 150 BPM."

An unreadable result means your ECG reading can’t be classified. This can happen if the signal does not meet the criteria for analysis. If you get an unreadable result, try taking the ECG reading again following the instructions carefully for best results.

"Take regular ECGs to stay proactive about your heart health. Doctors can use ECGs to gain insights about your heart rhythm and look for irregularities.
If you believe you’re having a heart attack or a medical emergency, call emergency services."
